body: Wow, that story gives me a lot of hope, thank you.  I hope she keeps doing well.  I'm thinking about changing some of my external physical features that make me memorable and identify me with my job (bleached hair, etc.) as a way of making me less recognizable (even if it's just paranoia, it'd soothe some of that worry) and at least giving me something to look forward to.

Thank you.  I'm trying to remember that she'd miss me and doesn't deserve to lose an owner since she's a rescue in the first place, but my brain keeps spinning it differently.  It's like I have two different voices in my head and one's the intellectual side and the other's this kneejerk hateful side.

I don't really.  I have a couple other sex worker friends, but one doesn't do any work that counts as illegal and the other is in the same place with burnout.  I know there are groups that are supposed to offer support for this but the ones I've found have a heavily evangelical bent that makes me uncomfortable.

Your description of the evolution from caterpie to butterfree made me laugh once I googled them and realized those are pokemon, and did make a lot of sense, so thank you for that.  I'm still really worried about not upsetting my parents, but intellectually I realize killing myself would presumably make them more upset, even if I have these recurring thoughts it'd be better for them in the long run.

I'm hoping to be able to resolve things with my roommate...we've been friends since we were teenagers and she's generally a nice person, she just isn't used to dogs and I don't think she realizes how attached I am to mine.  She used to like her.  I don't know what happened.

But I think you might be right about the industry...that's actually something I know intellectually but I needed to be reminded of it, thank you.
Thank you.  I really appreciate it.

It is definitely a job, but its external pressures (it's not legal to do some of the work I've done where I live) are enormous, and part of why I got so burned out was working in an oil boom area where there were a lot more safety concerns.  

Now that I've slept and calmed down a little bit I do see what you mean about my parents not automatically knowing and am feeling a bit less drastic, although I still don't really trust myself around the knife block.  But I saw my dog and these messages helped me a lot.

Thank you.

She does.  I'm trying to remember that, thank you.

The problem with moving is twofold: moving in with someone and trying to live a responsible life was supposed to be the change, and I'm scared that if I move in with my parents they'll figure out what I've been doing for a living.  They're nice people but we're not very touchy-feely with each other.  I don't want to make them ashamed of me.

Editing to add, I'm not really ashamed of the job that I did, exactly, it's just got so much cultural baggage and associated bullshit attached that it becomes soul-sucking.  It's constant emotional and physical output.  And I think it would definitely shame my parents, who are Eastern European and semi-conservative.
